rfi.title: Resumption of $20bn Cabo Delgado gas project reignites both hope and resentment
rfi.description: The resumption of one of the world's biggest gas projects by French energy giant TotalEnergies, after a five-year suspension following a deadly jihadist attack, has raised hopes of jobs and prosperity in northern Mozambique. But this second instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – questions whether the country's vast gas wealth will benefit local communities.

rfi.title: Paris no longer carries the load as audit backs asylum redistribution plan
rfi.description: France's system for moving asylum seekers from the Paris region to other parts of the country has helped ease pressure on accommodation, but is not being used to its full potential and remains unevenly applied, according to the country's public spending watchdog.

rfi.title: Sudan rights groups blame RSF paramilitary for drone strikes that hit civilians
rfi.description: Drone strikes blamed on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have killed at least 23 civilians and wounded 19 others in the Sudanese city of El-Obeid, local monitoring groups have said, as the use of armed drones continues to spread across the country in its more than three-year war.

rfi.title: British art 'giant' David Hockney dies aged 88

rfi.title: Two French cities impose curfews for under-16s during World Cup
rfi.description: The mayors of Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand are imposing nighttime curfews on children under 16 during the 2026 World Cup. They say the move is aimed at preventing the violent unrest seen after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory last month.

rfi.title: Rise in adulterated cannabis in France, as edible CBD ban shakes industry
rfi.description: Cannabis use in France is once again under scrutiny, with a drugs monitor reporting a sharp rise in adulterated products on the illegal market, and risky new products entering the legal CBD market. To address the issue of mislabelled products, France has banned edible CBD products, raising concerns in the cannabis industry.

rfi.title: Ebola outbreak spreads in DRC as misinformation hampers response
rfi.description: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have launched an online campaign to tackle growing mistrust surrounding a deadly Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) says misinformation is hampering efforts to contain the haemorrhagic fever, which broke out in the eastern province of Ituri on 15 May.

rfi.title: Mexico brush past ill-disciplined South Africa to launch World Cup party

rfi.title: Children in danger 'not heard' in France, rights lawyer warns after Lyhanna death
rfi.description: The abduction and killing of 11-year-old French schoolgirl Lyhanna has catapaulted child protection to the top of France's political agenda – with President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday calling for full accountability and the government pledging full transparency. As investigators examine possible failures by the justice system, child rights lawyer Dominique Attias tells RFI professionals have been warning for years that vulnerable children are not being protected.

rfi.title: Killing of gay man to be investigated as homophobic crime following protests
rfi.description: Police investigating the murder of a young gay man in the eastern French city of Metz have said the case will now be treated as a homophobic crime, after protestations from rights groups and politicians.

rfi.title: RFI denounces violation of press freedom after French reporter barred by Israel
rfi.description: RFI has condemned Israel's decision to refuse entry to journalist Alice Froussard, describing the move as "an obstacle to press freedom". Froussard, who reports on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict for French media, including RFI, was turned away on arrival at Tel Aviv airport and sent back without explanation.

Cette fusion n’est « pas susceptible de nuire à la concurrence ni aux consommateurs américains », selon l’administration Trump. Une position contestée à Hollywood, où l’on redoute des licenciements massifs.

lemonde.title: Le « Trump Kennedy Center » doit redevenir simplement le Kennedy Center, maintient un juge fédéral à Washington

Le juge a aussi suspendu la fermeture pour deux ans du Kennedy Center pour rénovation décidée par la direction des lieux, sous l’influence du président américain.

lemonde.title: Les adieux du monde politique à Bernadette Chirac

lemonde.description: Energie, eau, métaux… la ruée vers l’intelligence artificielle s’accompagne d’une demande croissante en ressources, note une nouvelle étude.

zeit.title: Neues Album von Olivia Rodrigo: Auch Liebeskummer wird Routine
zeit.description: Das neue Album von Olivia Rodrigo sollte eigentlich einmal für die heitere Seite des Verliebtseins werben – das ist ihr nicht ganz gelungen, sonst aber alles.

zeit.title: USA: Trumps Name wird von Kennedy Center entfernt
zeit.description: Der US-Präsident hatte seinen Namen am Kulturzentrum anbringen lassen. Per Gerichtsbeschluss montierten ihn Arbeiter nun wieder ab. Das Schauspiel wurde live übertragen.

zeit.title: Holunderblütenpfannkuchen: Da duftet die Küche plötzlich nach Urlaub
zeit.description: Diese Pfannkuchen mit Holunderblüten und Erdbeeren sind so gut, dass sie schon verputzt sind, bevor der Frühstückstisch gedeckt ist. Schmecken eben nach Provence!

zeit.title: Frührente: Bereuen Sie die Frührente?
zeit.description: Viele romantisieren die Rente, hören früh auf zu arbeiten und merken dann, dass etwas fehlt. Wie ist es für Sie, nicht mehr im Betrieb zu sein? Berichten Sie uns davon!

zeit.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Das war die WM-Nacht
zeit.description: Die USA sind furios in die Heim-WM gestartet. Kanada hat gegen Bosnien-Herzegowina den ersten Punkt bei einer Weltmeisterschaft überhaupt geholt. Die Spielberichte

zeit.description: Ein Abkommen könnte »in den kommenden Tagen« unterzeichnet werden, sagte Irans Außenminister. Die US-Armee hat in der Nacht iranische Drohnen abgeschossen. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Bayern gegen Alba: Schwärmereien nach Final-Auftakt: «Festival für Basketball»
Irankrieg: Wie sich im Iran die Angriffslogik verschiebt

Landesregierung: Was der Sticker auf dem Handy von Olaf Lies bedeutet

Invasive Insekten: Invasive Blutsauger könnten künftig auch den Norden befallen

Sachbücher für den Urlaub: Vier fantastische Sachbücher für den Sommer
zeit.description: Die Seele Großbritanniens, die Zukunft der Alpen und die Geschichte eines Wohnhauses in Paris. Diese Sachbücher sollten Sie unbedingt mit in den Urlaub nehmen.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les États-Unis écrasent le Paraguay pour leur entrée en lice
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont largement dominé le Paraguay (4-1), vendredi à Los Angeles pour leur premier match du Mondial 2026 dont ils sont coorganisateurs. Les Américains prennent provisoirement les commandes du groupe D, avant le match entre la Turquie et l'Australie à Vancouver samedi.

france24fr.title: En direct : les États-Unis abattent des drones iraniens qui ciblaient des navires à Ormuz
france24fr.description: L'armée américaine a indiqué dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi avoir abattu plusieurs drones iraniens qui ciblaient des navires commerciaux dans le détroit d'Ormuz. Les États-Unis et l'Iran avaient déclaré vendredi être proches d'un accord pour mettre fin à leur conflit entamé le 28 février, un haut responsable américain avançant qu'un texte satisfaisant les deux parties avait été rédigé. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Conflit israélo-palestinien : la perspective d'une solution à deux États "se rétrécit"
france24fr.description: Des ONG palestiniennes et israéliennes ont affirmé vendredi, lors d'une réunion internationale à Paris, que "la fenêtre d'opportunité pour une solution (à deux États) demeure, mais elle se rétrécit". Le Premier ministre canadien a annoncé une contribution de 100 millions de dollars du Canada, dans le cadre de cette réunion, pour "une aide humanitaire urgente aux Palestiniens en Cisjordanie et à Gaza".

france24fr.title: L'Union européenne annonce la reprise, lundi, des négociations d'adhésion avec l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Les États membres de l'Union européenne ont décidé vendredi d'ouvrir à partir de lundi le premier des six "clusters" de négociations d'adhésion avec l'Ukraine et la Moldavie. Le président ukrainien a salué "un soutien politique et moral significatif pour notre État et notre peuple".

france24fr.title: RD Congo: Martin Fayulu blessé dans des affrontements au sit-in contre la réforme constitutionnelle
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, l’opposition poursuit sa mobilisation contre le projet de changement de la Constitution porté par la majorité au pouvoir. Elle accuse Félix Tshisekedi de vouloir se maintenir au pouvoir au-delà de son second mandat qui expire en 2028. L’opposition a appelé ses militants a tenir un sit-in à Kinshasa… Mobilisation dispersée par les forces de l’ordre.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : pour le premier match sur son sol, le Canada arrache le nul contre la Bosnie
france24fr.description: Le Canada, pays co-organisateur du Mondial 2026 avec le Mexique et les États-Unis, a arraché le nul 1-1 face à la Bosnie-Herzégovine vendredi à Toronto, pour le premier des 13 matches qui se dérouleront sur son sol.

france24fr.title: RDC : Fayulu et Sesanga blessés, l'opposition dénonce une dérive du pouvoir
france24fr.description:
La tension monte en République démocratique du Congo. Plusieurs opposants ont été blessés à Kinshasa lors d'une manifestation contre le projet de réforme constitutionnelle porté par la majorité présidentielle. L'opposition accuse le président Félix Tshisekedi de vouloir ouvrir la voie à un troisième mandat malgré les dispositions actuelles de la Constitution.
 
Patrick Mbamu, secrétaire exécutif de l'ECiDé France, le parti de Martin Fayulu, est l'invité du Journal de l'Afrique. Il revient sur le

france24fr.title: Guerre en Iran, affaire Lyhanna et une Coupe du Monde controversée
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis et l’Iran affichent leur optimisme et assurent n’avoir jamais été aussi proches d’un accord. En France, l’affaire Lyhanna, cette fillette de 11 ans retrouvée morte dans le Gers, provoque une vive émotion et une colère grandissante contre les dysfonctionnements de la justice. Enfin, l’événement sportif le plus suivi de la planète s'est ouvert hier dans un contexte géopolitique tendu...

france24fr.title: Amel Bent, la voix de la lumière
france24fr.description: Rendez-vous avec la star de la chanson Amel Bent. En vingt ans de carrière, Amel a écoulé plus d’un million d’albums et récolté de nombreux trophées. Avec sa capacité à fédérer tant le monde de la variété que celui de la musique urbaine, elle a su s’imposer comme l’une des figures principales de la pop française. Retour sur son enfance à La Courneuve, ainsi que son lien avec Charles Aznavour et le monde du rap. Dans cet épisode, LaCrim offre la vidéo surprise.

france24fr.title: Introduction de SpaceX en bourse : l'opération qui bat tous les records
france24fr.description: C'est une opération sans équivalent dans l'histoire de la finance. L'entreprise spatiale californienne SpaceX – création et propriété d'Elon Musk – fait ses premiers pas sur le marché d'actions américain avec des chiffres stratosphériques : 555 millions d'actions et une valorisation estimée entre 1 765 et 2 000 milliards de dollars, soit près de cent fois le chiffre d'affaires de l'entreprise en 2025. Pourquoi un tel engouement ? Risque-t-on une bulle spatiale ?

france24fr.title: Edi Rama parle "d'ingérence iranienne" contre le projet immobilier des Trump
france24fr.description: Cette semaine, nous recevons Edi Rama, Premier ministre albanais. Il commente les manifestations qui secouent son pays contre la construction d'un complexe hôtelier de luxe lié à la famille Trump.

france24fr.title: Accord "imminent" avec l’Iran ? Trump brouille les pistes avec ses revirements incessants
france24fr.description: Après avoir affirmé la veille qu'un accord avec l'Iran pourrait être signé dans les prochains jours pour mettre fin à la guerre, Donald Trump a changé de ton vendredi, accusant Téhéran de mentir. Une séquence qui résume à elle seule les profondes incertitudes entourant les négociations et leurs chances d'aboutir après plus de quatre mois de conflit. Décryptage.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Maroc de Hakimi se prépare avant son match contre le Brésil
france24fr.description:
À moins de deux jours de son premier match contre le Brésil, le Maroc se prépare dans son camp de base à Basking Ridge, dans le New Jersey. La sélection a dû
 
essuyer plusieurs coups durs avec les forfaits de deux joueurs clés mais ses supporters restent optimistes. Crédit musique : George Van Dyk.

france24fr.title: Xénophobie en Afrique du Sud : un climat de peur qui s’accentue avant l’ultimatum du 30 juin
france24fr.description: Le Nigeria, le Ghana et le Malawi ont rapatrié ces derniers jours plusieurs centaines de ressortissants depuis l’Afrique du Sud, craignant pour leur sécurité après de violentes manifestations contre les immigrés. Un climat de peur entretenu par des groupes xénophobes qui exigent le départ des étrangers illégaux d'ici la fin du mois de juin.

france24fr.title: "Zeroers" : quand la Russie récompense la brutalité de ses commandants
france24fr.description: Le colonel Ramil Faskhoutdinov est devenu vendredi "héros de la Russie" à l’occasion de la fête nationale russe. Un honneur pour ce commandant accusé à de multiples reprises de brutalité extrême contre ses hommes et qui représente la figure du "zeroer", terme jargonneux désignant un chef militaire qui s’arroge un droit de vie et de mort sur les soldats qu’il commande.

france24fr.title: Arménie, le choix de l'Europe ?
france24fr.description: Quelle marge de manœuvre pour Nikol Pachinian après la victoire de son parti, Contrat civil, aux dernières législatives en Arménie ? Si la victoire consacre l'orientation impulsée par le Premier ministre depuis 2018, elle est vue par certains comme un défi à Moscou qui conserve quelques leviers de pression. Nikol Pachinian, qui s'est rapproché des Occidentaux, a cherché à régler le conflit avec l'Azerbaïdjan et à préserver ses liens avec la Russie tout en s'émancipant de Moscou. Les élections lé

france24fr.title: Des centres de retour pour migrants hors de l'UE : un pacte anti-migration ?
france24fr.description: La politique migratoire de l'Union européenne (UE) mise en œuvre en ce mois de juin se durcit. Après des années de débats, le Pacte asile et migration va s'appliquer. Cet ensemble législatif est censé instaurer une solidarité entre les Vingt-Sept pour répartir les demandeurs d'asile et aussi accélérer l'examen des dossiers en prévoyant un filtrage aux frontières extérieures de l'Union européenne dans des zones de transit.

france24fr.title: VSS : la France face aux dysfonctionnements de sa justice
france24fr.description: C'est une France sous le choc qui découvre l'ampleur des dysfonctionnements de sa justice. La mort de la petite Lyhanna, onze ans, a pris le pays aux tripes lorsque le profil du principal suspect a été connu… Jérôme Barella, père de famille "sans histoire" traînait en réalité plaintes et signalements à son encontre, pour attouchements et viols, depuis 2017 sans jamais avoir été convoqué par les autorités. La multiplication des témoignages de femmes contre Patrick Bruel arrive dans la même périod

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Krieg in der Ukraine dauert nun länger als der Erste Weltkrieg – die neue globale Ordnung prägt er bereits nachhaltig
nzz.description: Im Kampf um die Ukraine geht es um weit mehr als Osteuropa. Seit  Trumps Amtsantritt ist das Eskalationspotenzial weiter angestiegen. Es profitieren aber nicht zwingend die Grossmächte.

nzz.title: Zu wenige AKW-Fachleute: Bleibt das Neubauverbot bestehen, wackelt auch der Langzeitbetrieb von Gösgen und Leibstadt
nzz.description: Kernenergie-Spezialisten sind bereits heute rar. Fehlt dem Nachwuchs in der Schweiz die Perspektive, ist der längerfristige Weiterbetrieb der bestehenden Atomkraftwerke in Gefahr.

nzz.title: WM-Flop 2022, Krieg, Hausarrest und Qualifikation in extremis: Vor dem Spiel gegen die Schweiz spricht wenig für Katar
nzz.description: Die Fussballer aus dem kleinen Wüstenstaat stürzten vor vier Jahren an ihrem Heimturnier ab. Jetzt wollen sie Wiedergutmachung. Doch die Vorzeichen sind schlecht.

nzz.title: Bis zu 150 Euro für ein WM-Trikot: So lukrativ ist das Geschäft für Adidas und Puma
nzz.description: Mit immer neuen Varianten heizen die Hersteller die Nachfrage an, hohe Preise schrecken die Konsumenten kaum ab. Ein Faktor lässt sich aber nicht kalkulieren.

nzz.title: Suspendierung von Karim Khan wegen Verdachts auf sexuelle Übergriffe: Dem Internationalen Strafgerichtshof stellen sich unangenehme Fragen
nzz.description: Die Haftbefehle gegen Netanyahu und Putin haben den ICC politisch exponiert. Seit der Chefankläger die Arbeit niedergelegt hat, steckt das Gericht erst recht in der Schwebe. Sind Verfahren nun blockiert?

nzz.title: Anthropic-Börsengang: Eine Basler Gruppe gehört zu den frühesten Investoren des wertvollsten KI-Startups der Welt
nzz.description: Der Verein Macroscopic Ventures warnt vor KI-Risiken und landet gleichzeitig mit einer eigenen KI-Investition einen Volltreffer. Das Aktienpaket der effektiven Altruisten aus Basel dürfte heute ein Vielfaches wert sein.

nzz.title: Vier verbrannte Erdbeerpflücker erinnern daran, was in Italiens Landwirtschaft schiefläuft
nzz.description: Anfang Juni kommt es in Süditalien zu einer grausamen Tat. Sie gibt einen Einblick in ein längst bekanntes Problem.

nzz.title: Die Satelliten von Starlink haben die Kriegsführung verändert. Doch das ist erst der Anfang: SpaceX wird noch wichtiger
nzz.description: Kriege werden künftig auch im Weltall entschieden. Das macht SpaceX zum bedeutenden Partner des amerikanischen Militärs.

nzz.title: Einst waren die Huthi eine Erweckungsbewegung. Jetzt herrschen sie über ein halbes Land
nzz.description: Nach der Eskalation Anfang Juni drohen auch noch die Huthi aufseiten Irans in den Nahostkrieg einzugreifen. Dabei könnten sie grossen Schaden anrichten. Aber wer sind die Huthi eigentlich?

nzz.title: Ballsaal, Triumphbogen und «Trump Promenade» – der Präsident baut seine Hauptstadt um
nzz.description: Am 14. Juni feiert Donald Trump seinen 80. Geburtstag. Ein Rundgang durch Washington zeigt, wie sich der amerikanische Präsident als Bauherr zu verewigen sucht.

nzz.title: Die Welt ist ein Buch und das Dasein ein Spiel mit dem Chaos: Warum James Joyces «Finnegans Wake» das Leben ein bisschen leichter macht
nzz.description: James Joyces letzter Roman gilt als schwierig, fast unlesbar. Dabei hilft er, die Gegenwart besser zu verstehen.

nzz.title: Acht tote Elefanten: Das klingt verdächtig
nzz.description: Ungewöhnlich viele Elefanten sind seit 2020 im Zürcher Zoo gestorben, darunter auch neugeborene Kälber. Geht es Elefanten im Zoo gut genug, um sich fortpflanzen zu können?

nzz.title: Viel Angst vor wenig Gift: warum wir uns vor der Nosferatu-Spinne fürchten
nzz.description: Spinnenbisse mit schlimmeren Folgen als ein Wespenstich sind hierzulande eine Rarität. Warum ist die Angst davor trotzdem so verbreitet? Die Kolumne «Hauptsache, gesund».

nzz.title: «Mein Ziel ist, die Analysten auf neue Ideen zu bringen», sagt der ETH-Forscher, der an der Fussball-WM die Gegner der Schweizer Nati mathematisch zerlegt
nzz.description: Für Ulrik Brandes ist Fussball ein Gebietseroberungsspiel. Sein Analysetool entlarvt die Taktik ganzer Teams auf einen Blick.

nzz.title: Kritische Rohstoffe: Mit ihrer bisherigen Strategie bleibt die EU vom chinesischen Wohlwollen abhängig
nzz.description: Für das Rüstungswesen und die Industrie ist das Reich der Mitte der mit Abstand wichtigste Lieferant. Die EU will das ändern, doch sie macht kaum Fortschritte. Die USA setzen hingegen aufs Tempo.

nzz.title: Was könnte sich Elon Musk mit seinem neuen Reichtum kaufen? Eine fiktive Shoppingtour durch die Schweiz
nzz.description: Elon Musk ist der erste Dollar-Billionär der Geschichte. Was kann man sich mit so viel Geld leisten? Jede Menge, wie ein Blick auf Schweizer Wahrzeichen und Traditionsunternehmen zeigt.

observador.title: Mauricio fez de Ted e pôs o Lasso para a Missão Impossível
observador.description: Os EUA deram o primeiro passo rumo à conquista do Mundial, objetivo assumido por Pochettino. Equipa da casa dominou um frágil Paraguai com Pulisic, Balogun e Reyna em grande plano (4-1).

observador.title: 4h. EUA abatem vários drones iranianos no Estreito de Ormuz
observador.description: É o que adianta o Comando Central dos Estados Unidos numa publicação na rede social X. Ainda, os Estados Unidos venceram o Paraguai por 4-1 no primeiro jogo do grupo D do mundial de futebol.

observador.title: 3h. CGTP. Há "condições" para derrubar pacote laboral
observador.description: A discussão da proposta está marcada para o dia 18 de junho. Ainda, Pedro Proença considera que a seleção portuguesa tem qualidade e bons jogadores.

observador.title: "Convidei os jogadores a visitarem a comunidade portuguesa"
observador.description: A Seleção já está no hotel em Palm Beach. Portugueses, americanos e até colombianos, vestidos a rigor, apoiaram sem direito a fotos ou autógrafos, mas com convites: "visitem a nossa comunidade".

observador.title: 2h. Pedro Proença revela "grande ambição" da seleção
observador.description: O presidente da FPF considera que a equipa das quinas tem qualidade e bons jogadores. Ainda, o secretário-geral da CGTP diz que estão reunidas "todas as condições" para o pacote laboral ser derrotado

observador.title: Os assobios ao Irão e a estrela Perry: a última cerimónia
observador.description: A capital mundial do entretenimento esteve à altura do certame, ainda que a primeira parte tivesse o estádio bastante despido. Bandeira do Irão foi assobiado e Katy Perry brilhou em "casa"

observador.title: 1h. A seleção portuguesa já chegou a Miami
observador.description: E realiza este sábado o primeiro treino em solo norte-americano. Ainda, o memorando de entendimento entre o Irão e os Estados Unidos parece estar cada vez mais próximo.

observador.title: Fator C, de casa e de... campeão: Benfica vence Sporting
observador.description: No primeiro dérbi da final, o Benfica brilhou através das individualidades, com Diego Nunes e Léo Gugiel a transcenderem-se frente ao rival. Reação do Sporting esbarrou nos ferros (2-1).

observador.title: Justiça dos EUA aprova compra da Warner Bros pela Paramount
observador.description: Justiça norte-americana considera que fusão entre estúdios "não resultará em prejuízo para a concorrência ou para os consumidores". Decisão enfrenta oposição de muitos na indústria do entretenimento.

observador.title: Setúbal rejeita acusações do BE sobre Herdade da Comenda
observador.description: BE acusou a Herdade da Comenda de se apropriar de cinco praias da Arrábida. Câmara de Setúbal justifica o condicionamento dos acessos com as derrocadas que colocam as estradas em risco.

observador.title: Setúbal quer transporte marítimo para as praias da Arrábida
observador.description: Autarquia quer desenvolver o projeto em 2027. O custo da construção de infraestruturas de apoio aos transportes e a recuperação dos estragos provocados pelas derrocadas está estimado em 50 milhões.

observador.title: Orçamento da UE dá mais 1,6 mil milhões a Portugal
observador.description: A presidência cipriota propõe que Portugal receba cerca de 35 mil milhões até 2034, mais 1,6 mil milhões do que a Comissão Europeia propôs. Miranda Sarmento fala em "longo caminho".

observador.title: Homem de 50 anos morre após mergulhar no rio Douro no Porto
observador.description: Tinha cerca de 50 anos. O alerta foi dado às 19h54 de sexta-feira. Apesar de ser um salto de pouca altura, a vítima ficou inanimada debaixo de água.

observador.title: Itália nega extradição de Zambelli por parcialidade do STF
observador.description: Zambelli, voz radical da extrema-direita no Brasil, foi condenada pelo Tribunal brasileiro a 10 anos de prisão. Tribunal de Itália considerou que o juíz Alexandre de Moraes interferiu na decisão.

observador.title: Queixa de filho revela mais de 70 contas de Pinto da Costa
observador.description: Queixa-crime do filho denuncia desvio do património e esvaziamento das contas bancárias do pai nas vésperas da morte. Mas levantamentos terão começado ainda antes do casamento com a última mulher.

observador.title: Alguém pode escrever um tricolon com anáfora ao Presidente?
observador.description: No 10 de Junho, ficou provado mais uma vez que os nossos políticos acham que um discurso se insere na mesma família retórica de uma lista de compras de supermercado. Não tinha de ser assim.

observador.title: O Mundial comanda o sonho
observador.description: Os portugueses vão sonhar. Aliás, o nosso problema não é a falta de sonhos: é nunca acordar.

observador.title: ULS de Lisboa ativam planos de contingência para o calor
observador.description: Loures-Odivelas e Lisboa Ocidental em alerta amarelo; São José, Santa Maria e Amadora-Sintra em vigilância reforçada. SNS alerta para riscos em idosos e doentes crónicos.

letemps.title: «C’est à travers le sumo qu’on peut comprendre la profondeur de la culture japonaise»: mi-juin, ce sport traditionnel investira Paris
letemps.description:
Les lutteurs disputent un tournoi dans la capitale française, les 13 et 14 juin. Une délocalisation étonnante pour ces poids lourds, habituellement cantonnés au Japon. L’occasion de se rendre à Tokyo pour voir si les signes de détente de cet univers rigide sont bien réels

letemps.description:
Epidémie d’Ebola, développement de l’intelligence artificielle, préparation aux futures pandémies… l’Organisation mondiale de la santé est confrontée à de multiples défis, alors même que ses moyens sont de plus en plus limités. letemps.description:
Le football, qui ne vit bientôt plus que par les records des buteurs, aura bien du mal à faire mieux que les 13 buts en cinq matchs de l’avant-centre de l’équipe de France. A l’époque, cela lui rapporta… un fusil de chasse

letemps.title: Scandale PrimeEnergy: la piste d’une escroquerie luxembourgeoise
letemps.description:
Les procureurs chargés de la faillite de la société genevoise active dans le photovoltaïque ont élargi leur accusation à des opérations financières menées depuis le Grand-Duché. L’actionnaire principal blâme la Finma et Bertrand Picard. Les victimes peuvent espérer récupérer entre 25 et 45% de leur mise, a annoncé le liquidateur de la société.

phys-org.title: Lab-grown canine muscle cells offer solution for early therapeutic testing
phys-org.description: Before testing new therapies in animals, researchers now have a more efficient starting point—lab-grown canine muscle cells that can help identify what works and what doesn't.

phys-org.title: Faster biological aging consistently linked to poverty and discrimination
phys-org.description: By integrating findings from 140 studies and nearly 66,000 individuals, researchers from the Biosocial team at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development in collaboration with Columbia University in New York have shown that lower socioeconomic status and exposure to discrimination are consistently associated with accelerated biological aging, measured in the epigenome.

phys-org.title: Meet REMORA: The autonomous space fleet built to tag and track asteroids
phys-org.description: To truly understand what an asteroid is made of, we need to send a probe to it. Remote sensing from ground-based telescopes, or even orbiting observatories, can only do so much. A new white paper submitted to the U.K. Space Agency's 2035 Space Frontiers program (available on the arXiv preprint server) pitches just such a mission architecture. phys-org.title: Solar geoengineering could shield up to 75% of oceans from heat waves
phys-org.description: Most people have experienced a heat wave on land. But heat waves can strike in the ocean too. And as the planet continues to warm, marine heat waves are growing longer and deadlier, hurting the seafood supply that billions of people worldwide rely on for their food and livelihoods.

phys-org.title: Gulf Stream shifted north during 12,900-year-old cold snap, first direct evidence shows
phys-org.description: During an abrupt global cold snap nearly 13,000 years ago, the Gulf Stream ocean current shifted farther north, temporarily disrupting eastern Canada's oceanic ecosystems, a process that could happen again as the climate changes, a new study by UCL researchers finds.

phys-org.title: Jurassic viral gene may have helped apple snails start laying eggs on land
phys-org.description: Pomacea canaliculata, commonly known as the apple snail, is a pest commonly found in Hong Kong's wetlands and farmlands. It feeds on aquatic plants and produces toxic pink egg masses resembling miniature grapes that adhere to plants or stone bunds. It is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) among 100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species.

phys-org.title: New species of Middle Miocene bear-dog described in tribute to Salvador Moyà-Solà
phys-org.description: A research team with the participation of the Institut Català de Paleontologia Miquel Crusafont (ICP) has described a new species of extinct carnivore from fossil remains recovered at the Els Casots site (Subirats, Alt Penedès). The study, published in the Journal of Mammalian Evolution, describes Paludocyon moyasolai, a medium-sized amphicyonid that lived approximately 15.9 million years ago, during the early Middle Miocene. The specific epithet "moyasolai" pays tribute to Salvador Moyà-Solà, a

phys-org.title: Scientist creates 'mini‑universe' to measure time without a clock
phys-org.description: A University of Birmingham scientist has built a "mini-universe" that takes a step toward answering one of science's biggest questions: "What is time?" Publishing his findings in Physical Review Research, Professor Giovanni Barontini shows how it is possible to measure the flow of time without using a clock at all. The new findings provide a scientific model in which a version of time emerges from the experiment itself.

phys-org.title: Mountainous landscapes store far more carbon than previously thought, new research shows
phys-org.description: Hilly and mountainous landscapes have a much greater ability to store carbon in the soil than previously thought, according to a new study co-led by scientists at the University of Oregon.

phys-org.title: Trees may store less carbon than expected in the future
phys-org.description: It's intuitive to think that if a tree is photosynthesizing, it's also growing. But that's not necessarily so—and a new study of oak trees, published in the journal Science Advances, found that even as they photosynthesize late into the year, their growth stops by midsummer.

phys-org.title: Supercomputer predicts 2026 World Cup results
phys-org.description: A model built by researchers from the University of Liverpool's Management School predicts an England-Spain FIFA World Cup 2026 final, with Spain the favorite to lift the trophy—a repeat of recent major tournament history. The supercomputer correctly predicted England's second-place finish at Euro 2024.

phys-org.title: Molecular anchors on gut phages could open new therapeutic avenues
phys-org.description: Bacteriophages, or phages, are viruses that infect bacteria and are not considered human pathogens. Yet researchers at the Translational Microbiology Laboratory of the Institute of Biochemistry, HUN-REN Biological Research Centre, Szeged, have shown that some gut phages can also physically interact with human cells. Their study identifies phage surface proteins that act as molecular anchors, promoting attachment to human cells, cellular uptake, and prolonged retention in the gastrointestinal tra

phys-org.title: Rare-earth-free zinc oxide achieves a first in stress-to-light conversion
phys-org.description: Mechanoluminescent materials convert mechanical energy such as stress, strain and vibration directly into light, making them attractive as self-powered sensors that require no batteries or wiring. From biomedical sensors to self-powered infrastructure monitoring sensors, mechanoluminescent materials have a wide range of potential applications. However, high-performance mechanoluminescent materials have traditionally relied on expensive rare-earth materials or complex material compositions.

phys-org.title: Novel forecasting model developed to predict river temperature
phys-org.description: The temperature of rivers is something most people think about only if they plan to go swimming, kayaking or spend a day fishing. Few consider how it could potentially affect their electricity bill.

phys-org.title: Landscape water velocities across Europe reshape nitrogen pollution risk under climate change
phys-org.description: Nitrate pollution is a growing global environmental challenge due to the extensive use of fertilizer. A study published in Science, led by the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries (IGB) with the Helmholtz Center for Environmental Research (UFZ), shows that both the amount of water moving through landscapes and how fast it moves play a key role in nitrogen pollution risk.

phys-org.title: Nuclear clocks tick for the first time
phys-org.description: Two independent research teams have achieved a longstanding goal in physics: building a working nuclear clock. The devices, developed by Beichen Huang and colleagues at Tsinghua University and by Luca Toscani De Col and colleagues at the Vienna Center for Quantum Science and Technology in Austria, exploit the nucleus of a thorium-229 atom to keep time with extraordinary precision—possibly surpassing even the best atomic clocks available today.

phys-org.title: Carbon dioxide unlocks safer oxidation chemistry under room-temperature conditions
phys-org.description: Oxidation reactions are indispensable to the chemical industry, but from a process safety perspective, they are among the most challenging transformations. A research team at the University of Bayreuth, working in collaboration with international partners, has now introduced a fundamentally new approach to oxidation reactions in which carbon dioxide is used as the oxygen source for chemical synthesis. This makes the reaction both safer and more sustainable. The researchers report on this new app

phys-org.title: Horse owners' personality and attachment style shape how they interact with and care for their horses
phys-org.description: A new study shows that horse owners' psychological characteristics, including their attachment styles and personality traits, are systematically linked to how frequently they ride, train, and spend quality time with their horses, as well as the equipment they choose to use. The findings offer new insights into how human psychology shapes horse welfare and management.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

proj-syn.title: Inequality in Évian
proj-syn.description: The G7 summit must recognize that extreme disparities in income, wealth, opportunity, and political influence are not only a defining feature of the global economy but also a major factor in many other shared challenges. For too long, the issue has been treated as a symptom rather than a cause.

proj-syn.title: Europeans Are the G7’s Grownups
proj-syn.description: Slowly but surely, the European Union is taking steps to reduce its current-account surplus and direct more of its substantial savings into domestic investment and growth. proj-syn.title: Modi Is Rigging Indian Democracy
proj-syn.description: Under the guise of routine voter-roll maintenance, India’s Election Commission has purged tens of millions of voters, disproportionately affecting opposition strongholds, the poor, and Muslim minorities. The result is an electoral system increasingly designed to favor the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

proj-syn.title: Learning to Govern a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: As the postwar multilateral order gives way to a multipolar and more contested world, global governance must adapt or risk irrelevance. The upcoming G7 summit offers a unique opportunity to champion a coalition-based approach that translates shared interests into collective action.

proj-syn.title: Cognition for Sale
proj-syn.description: AI is doing what no previous technology could, turning tacit human knowledge into a product that can be extracted, priced, and distributed at scale. Yet the same technology that democratizes cognitive labor may also weaken the human capacities on which complex societies depend.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech Gets Bigger
proj-syn.description: Recent stock-market gyrations are a reminder of just how dependent the United States and global economies have become on investors’ seemingly insatiable appetite for tech stocks. Even if a major correction is in the offing, however, it will not happen before SpaceX’s massive initial public offering draws in yet more leveraged investment, nor will it destroy the market power of the other tech giants that have spent years perfecting anti-competitive tactics that largely escape regulators’ purvi

proj-syn.title: The Democrats Need a Story, Not More Lists
proj-syn.description: Whereas Donald Trump has offered voters a clear and compelling narrative, Democrats have provided only vague aspirations and long lists of policies. To win over voters—rather than scrounging protest votes—they must articulate a compelling economic vision, with wage-led growth as its foundation.

proj-syn.title: What if Europe Loses Access to Its Climate Data?
proj-syn.description: The European Green Deal runs on data, from corporate disclosures to climate-risk analyses and decarbonization pathways. But much of this data feeds platforms and tools developed outside the European Union, which could threaten the bloc’s climate agenda and even its foundational values.

proj-syn.title: Raising Interest Rates Won’t Stabilize African Inflation
proj-syn.description: Monetary tightening in Africa would not only fail to rein in inflation; it would raise the cost of productive investment, suppress growth, and hamper the continent's much-needed structural transformation. A better strategy would focus on accelerating this transformation by channeling finance into productive industries.

proj-syn.title: Peak Oil Demand Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: Amid the disruptions caused by the US/Israeli-Iran war, countries have begun adapting to life with less oil. What started as a supply shock has become a demand story, forcing the energy sector to reconsider one of its most important assumptions: continued growth of global oil demand.

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. Yet income convergence with advanced economies has been painfully slow—and in most cases absent.

proj-syn.title: Is the US Stock Market Too Big?
proj-syn.description: With China and India having grown so fast as to compensate for the underperformance of their fellow BRICS (Brazil, Russia, and South Africa), the center of gravity in the global economy continues to shift eastward. The question now is whether—and when—equity valuations will reflect this underlying reality.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.
